title: Count paths through a grid moving right or down
summary: A robot can only move right or down; the ways into any square are the ways from above plus the ways from the left.
goal: Count the different routes from the top-left to the bottom-right corner

mapping.formal: One step right or one step down

examples.label: 1 by 1
examples.explanation: Already at the corner: one route, doing nothing.

ladder.name: Walk every route
ladder.idea: Recursively try moving right and moving down from each square, counting routes that reach the corner.

ladder.name: Write a note in every square
ladder.idea: The first row and column have one route each. Every other square's note is the note above plus the note to the left.
ladder.insight: The last move into a square comes from above or from the left, so its routes are the routes into those two squares, already written down.

ladder.name: Keep only one row of notes
ladder.idea: Each row only needs the row above it, so update a single row in place, left to right.
ladder.insight: When filling a row, the old value at a position is the note from above and the new value to its left is the note from the left, so one row holds both.

transfer.problem: A delivery bike in a city of one-way streets can only ride east or south. How many routes lead from the depot to a customer?
transfer.explanation: Routes into each junction are routes from the north plus routes from the west: the same grid table.

selfCheck: Gives the first row and column one route each.
Adds the note above and the note to the left.
Uses one row of notes in the final version.
